items.title: 8.8.1 Equilibrium constant expressions of some important reactions

source_refs.note: Topic 8.8.1, printed pages 174-176; Sample Problems 8.1 and 8.2 and Quick Check 8.4 (b) as the self-check.

blocks.text: Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water, CH3COOH(l) + C2H5OH(l) giving CH3COOC2H5(l) + H2O(l). At equilibrium 500 cm3 of the mixture contained 0.235 mol of ethanoic acid, 0.0350 mol of ethanol, 0.182 mol of ethyl ethanoate and 0.182 mol of water. Step 1, the concentrations in 0.5 dm3: 0.470, 0.070, 0.364 and 0.364 mol dm-3. Step 2, Kc = [CH3COOC2H5][H2O] / ([CH3COOH][C2H5OH]). Step 3, substitute: Kc = (0.364 x 0.0364) / (0.470 x 0.070) = 4.03 to three significant figures. Step 4, units: the mol dm-3 cancel, so Kc = 4.03 with no units.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The water concentration in the expression should be 0.364 mol dm-3, not 0.0364: Kc = (0.364 x 0.364) / (0.470 x 0.070) = 4.03, the book's answer.
Sample Problem 8.2: propanone and hydrogen cyanide

Propanone reacts with hydrogen cyanide, CH3COCH3(l) + HCN(g) giving CH3C(OH)(CN)CH3(l). A mixture of 0.0500 mol dm-3 propanone and 0.0500 mol dm-3 hydrogen cyanide reaches equilibrium at room temperature with a product concentration of 0.0233 mol dm-3. For every mole of product formed one mole of each reactant is consumed, so at equilibrium each reactant is 0.0500 - 0.0233 = 0.0267 mol dm-3. Kc = [product] / ([CH3COCH3][HCN]) = 0.0233 / (0.05 x 0.05) = 32.7 mol dm-3.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the reactants, 0.0267 mol dm-3 each, belong in the expression, not the starting 0.05: Kc = 0.0233 / (0.0267 x 0.0267) = 32.7. The unit is (mol dm-3)^-1, that is mol-1 dm3, not mol dm-3.
